draft.title: Jewish bioethics
card: Bioethics asks moral questions about medicine and life, such as euthanasia (ending a life to relieve suffering) and IVF (conceiving a child outside the body, then placing the embryo in the womb).
Judaism places great value on preserving life. Life is seen as a gift from God, so saving a life (pikuach nefesh) can override most religious laws.
Rabbis interpret the Torah and later teaching to apply it to new medical questions. Their rulings are called responsa, and different movements may reach different conclusions.
Most Jewish authorities oppose actively ending a life, including at the patient's request. Many support IVF, because having children is valued, though rabbis still debate how it should be done.
draft.remember: Jewish bioethics applies the value of preserving life through rabbinic interpretation, so rulings can differ.

a.q: Why do many Jewish authorities oppose active euthanasia?
opts: Life is a gift from God, so preserving it is highly valued
Suffering is seen as a punishment that must be endured
Medical treatment is forbidden by the Torah in most cases
Rabbis have no authority to rule on medical questions
a.why: The value placed on preserving life, which is seen as God's gift, leads most authorities to reject actively ending it. Suffering as punishment is tempting but is not the reason given on the card, and Judaism strongly supports healing.
a.clue: Think about how Judaism regards life itself.

b.q: Two rabbis from different Jewish movements give different rulings on a new IVF technique. What best explains this?
opts: They interpret the same sources and values in different ways
One rabbi rejects the value of preserving life
One rabbi's ruling has no link to the Torah
Judaism has no teaching on having children
b.why: Rabbinic interpretation applies shared values to new questions, and movements may reach different conclusions. The differences do not mean a rabbi has rejected the value of life, since both draw on it.
b.clue: Both rabbis start from the same values but apply them.
